title: Implement renameTo and createDirectory[AndParents] for RemoteActionFileSystem

timeline.message:
Implement renameTo and createDirectory[AndParents] for RemoteActionFileSystem

Fixes #16351.
timeline.author: Chi Wang

diff.patch:
@@ -572,6 +572,38 @@ EOF
   expect_log "test.outputs_manifest__MANIFEST"
 }
 
+function test_multiple_test_attempts() {
+  # Test that test logs of multiple test attempts can be renamed and reported by
+  # BEP.
+  mkdir -p a
+  cat > a/BUILD <<EOF
+sh_test(
+  name = "foo",
+  srcs = ["foo.sh"],
+)
+EOF
+  cat > a/foo.sh <<'EOF'
+exit 1
+EOF
+  chmod a+x a/foo.sh
+  rm -rf $TEST_TMPDIR/bep.json
+
+  bazel test \
+    --remote_executor=grpc://localhost:${worker_port} \
+    --remote_download_minimal \
+    --build_event_json_file=$TEST_TMPDIR/bep.json \
+    --flaky_test_attempts=2 \
+    //a:foo >& $TEST_log && fail "Test //a:foo should fail"
+
+  expect_log "FAILED in 2 out of 2"
+  expect_log "a/foo/test.log"
+  expect_log "a/foo/test_attempts/attempt_1.log"
+  cat $TEST_TMPDIR/bep.json > $TEST_log
+  rm -rf $TEST_TMPDIR/bep.json
+  expect_log "attempt\":1.*test.log.*bytestream.*test.xml.*bytestream"
+  expect_log "attempt\":2.*test.log.*bytestream.*test.xml.*bytestream"
+}
+
 # This test is derivative of test_bep_output_groups in
 # build_event_stream_test.sh, which verifies that successful output groups'
 # artifacts appear in BEP when a top-level target fails to build.

timeline.body: Should we assert that `sourcePath` and `targetPath` are under `outputBase`? (I can't imagine a legitimate use case for moving to or from a different root.) And in that case, do we ever need to fall back to the local filesystem?

reply.body: Added assertions for `sourcePath` and `targetPath`. Considering dynamic execution, both local and remote could have files so we need to try to rename on both. Also if the file is in the remote AND local (because it was staged), we need to keep them in sync.

timeline.body: Same as above - is it stricly necessary to create the directory in the local filesystem?

reply.body: yes, for dynamic execution AND for action logs.
